# pai now

Urgency window: this session's workers run with now (front + preempt local)

```
pai now [command] [options]
```

The operator's explicit instrumentation for urgency (the `/now` token in a prompt is the same switch). While a window is open, every worker this session starts runs with --now — ahead at the local engine, preempting the other local workers — and with where=local when it was opened with local. Workers already running when it opens are made urgent. `pai worker run --now` and `pai worker priority <id> now` are the per-worker forms. Workers never open a window themselves.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--session NAME|ID` | string | — | Session name or id (default: this session) |
| `--local` | flag | — | Those workers also run where=local |
| `--minutes N` | number | — | Window length in minutes (default 30) |
| `--clear` | flag | — | Close the window instead of opening it |

```sh
pai now
pai now --local --minutes 15
pai worker run --local -p 'fix the flake'
pai now --clear
```

See also: `pai worker ps`, `pai worker priority`

### pai now set

Open (or extend) the window (default verb)

```
pai now set [SESSION] [options]
```

Opens the window for this session, or for --session <name|id>. --local also forces where=local for those workers; --minutes N overrides the configured window (default 30). Prints one line: what is open until when.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SESSION` | no | Session name or id (default: this session) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--local` | flag | — | Those workers also run where=local |
| `--minutes N` | number | — | Window length in minutes (default: workers.urgency.windowMinutes, 30) |

```sh
pai now
pai now --local
pai now chat-7 --minutes 15
```

### pai now status

Show the open window (this session, or all on this machine)

```
pai now status [SESSION]
```

With a session argument shows that session's window; otherwise this session's, and when none is open here, every open window on this machine.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SESSION` | no | Session name or id |

```sh
pai now status
pai now status chat-7
```

### pai now clear

Close the window now

```
pai now clear [SESSION]
```

Closes this session's window (or --session's). Running workers keep their priority; change it with `pai worker priority <id> normal`.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SESSION` | no | Session name or id (default: this session) |

```sh
pai now --clear
pai now clear chat-7
```

## Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `pai now set` | Open (or extend) the window (default verb) |
| `pai now status` | Show the open window (this session, or all on this machine) |
| `pai now clear` | Close the window now |
